learningObjective: Trace how an HMM carries temporal dependence through a first-order hidden-state chain while each observation is generated only from its same-time state.
mediumRationale: A compact deterministic SVG is the smallest medium that can align four latent states with four observations, show transition and emission directions, and make the missing observation-to-observation edges meaningful. The same geometry also makes the factorization readable one local factor at a time.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected because automatic layout could obscure strict timestep alignment and make the absence of direct observation-to-observation edges less immediate.
mediumComparison.svg: Selected because fixed two-row geometry aligns each emission under its latent state and keeps the transition chain, local factors, and conditional-independence separator visible at phone width.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Rejected because a table can align states and observations but cannot naturally express directed dependence or d-separation through the latent chain.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected because sampling state paths and emissions would add controls and stochastic state without improving the single factorization objective.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected because canonical HMM sources contain state diagrams and trellises, but no external composition is needed and no permissive figure-reuse grant was established for the IEEE or textbook artwork. No source figure, notation layout, wording, data, or coordinates is copied.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected because prose lists the Markov and emission assumptions and gives their product, leaving readers to mentally infer which arrows exist, why observed values can still have long-range dependence, and what conditioning on a current state separates.

pages.insight: The preceding Message Passing slide motivates local inference from conditional independence but incorrectly over-identifies message passing with EM; it supplies context, not an HMM factorization.

The GMM/HMM slide distinguishes an HMM's switching dynamics from a GMM's independent categorical choice and lists evaluation, decoding, and training, but does not draw the latent-to-observed dependency structure.

The Forward-Backward slide states the key separator property: given the state at time k, observations on the two sides factorize. It focuses on inference and Baum-Welch rather than the model's generative graph.
The neighboring CRF slide moves to a discriminative undirected sequence model and dynamic-programming normalization, providing a contrast but no additional HMM generative structure.

The linear-factor-model slide places HMMs among latent time-series models and repeats that past and future observations are conditionally independent given the current state; its detailed equations concern linear Gaussian systems instead.

deckReview.notes: All 214 pages of the local PDF were text-indexed page by page for hidden Markov, HMM, Viterbi, Baum-Welch, forward-backward, latent state, emission, and Markov property. Pages 67-71 are the complete contiguous HMM teaching neighborhood and were read in full. Speech slides 122 and 124 mention HMM-based acoustic modeling, while page 126 discusses RNN-T; none adds the requested factorization. No deck pixels, artwork, code, prose, equations, data, coordinates, or layout is reused.

sources.title: A Tutorial on Hidden Markov Models and Selected Applications in Speech Recognition
sources.usage: Used as the canonical HMM tutorial to verify the first-order state process, observation independence conditioned on the current state, initial, transition, and emission parameters, the joint sequence probability, and the three classical problems.
sources.license: IEEE publication copyright applies and no permissive figure-reuse license was identified. No paper figure, numerical example, prose, notation layout, or artwork is reproduced; the shipped diagram is an original factorization schematic.

sources.title: hmmlearn Tutorial
sources.usage: Used as official implementation documentation to cross-check that observations are generated by internal hidden states, hidden transitions form a first-order Markov chain, emissions condition on the current state, and pi, A, and emission parameters determine the HMM.
sources.license: The hmmlearn repository uses the BSD 3-Clause license. The documentation is cited for semantics only; no documentation prose, code, example values, image, or layout is copied.

sources.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction
sources.usage: Used as an authoritative textbook cross-check for directed graphical-model factorization, conditional independence, state-space models, filtering and smoothing, and hidden Markov models.
sources.license: The official MIT Press page provides access and supplemental resources but does not state a blanket permissive license for book figures. No textbook figure, prose, data, code, or layout is adapted.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only mental model is that first-order refers to the latent dynamics, not to independence of the observations. In the original four-step schematic, each z_t receives an arrow only from z_(t-1), and each x_t receives an arrow only from z_t. Thus the local factors are pi(z1), p(x1|z1), then p(z_t|z_(t-1))p(x_t|z_t). Observations at distant times may remain dependent through the unobserved state path, while conditioning on an intermediate latent state separates past from future. Arrow direction, row position, node shape, direct labels, and a dashed separator carry every distinction without color.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, text-indexed all 214 deck pages and inspected the exact HMM neighborhood, then checked the canonical IEEE tutorial, official hmmlearn documentation, and an authoritative probabilistic-ML textbook before selecting an original generative-factorization SVG distinct from the existing inference-algorithm visual.

implementation.accessibility: The SVG has a linked title and detailed description naming every state, observation, transition, emission, factor, and separator implication. Hidden states use circles, observations use rounded rectangles, all arrows are directed and text-labelled, and the absence of horizontal observation edges is explicitly stated, so color is not required. The 360-unit viewBox uses the established plot-panel primitive without a minimum width for readability at 390 CSS pixels; existing theme variables preserve dark-mode contrast and shared print rules force a light high-contrast palette.
